text: My card isn't lost or stolen, it's right here in my wallet, but the chip seems dead and no card machine will read it at all.
label: card_not_working
rationale: The customer says outright that the card is not lost and describes a physical card that won't work, so lost_or_stolen_card is ruled out.

text: Please don't cancel anything, I'm happy with the payment I sent. I just want to know how many working days an international transfer normally takes.
label: transfer_timing
rationale: The customer rules out cancelling and asks how long a transfer takes to arrive.

text: Not trying to close my account or anything, I've just moved house and need to update my address on the app.
label: edit_personal_details
rationale: Closing the account is explicitly ruled out; the real request is to change an address.

text: My phone wasn't stolen, I've still got it in my hand, I just forgot my app passcode and now I'm locked out.
label: passcode_forgotten
rationale: The customer still has the phone and has only forgotten the passcode, so lost_or_stolen_phone does not apply.

text: This isn't about a transfer fee. I got charged a fee for taking cash out of an ATM yesterday and I want to know why.
label: cash_withdrawal_charge
rationale: The customer rules out a transfer fee; the fee was for an ATM cash withdrawal.

text: The ATM didn't swallow my card, it gave it straight back, but it only dispensed £60 when I asked for £100. Not happy.
label: wrong_amount_of_cash_received
rationale: The card came back; the complaint is that the ATM gave out the wrong amount of cash.

text: I'm not saying I don't recognise the payment, it's my coffee from this morning, but it's come out of my account twice.
label: transaction_charged_twice
rationale: The customer recognises the payment, so the problem is being charged twice, not an unrecognised payment.

text: I don't need to order a physical card, I already have one. I'd just like a virtual card as well for online shopping, how do I get it?
label: getting_virtual_card
rationale: Ordering a physical card is ruled out and the customer asks how to get a virtual card.

text: My top-up didn't fail, it actually went through and showed in my balance, but then it got reverted the next day. What happened?
label: top_up_reverted
rationale: The top-up succeeded and was then reversed, which is top_up_reverted, not a failed top-up.

text: I'm not asking about exchange fees, I just want to see what rate you're giving for euros today.
label: exchange_rate
rationale: Fees are explicitly ruled out; the customer wants the current exchange rate.

text: The transfer isn't pending anymore, the app says completed, but my landlord insists he still hasn't received the rent money.
label: transfer_not_received_by_recipient
rationale: The transfer shows as completed but the recipient has not received it, so pending_transfer is ruled out.

text: I don't need help activating my card, that's done. I just want to know if it's a Visa or a Mastercard.
label: visa_or_mastercard
rationale: Activation is already done; the only question is whether the card is Visa or Mastercard.

text: It's not contactless that's the problem, tapping my card works fine. It's Google Pay that refuses to add my card.
label: apple_pay_or_google_pay
rationale: Contactless is said to work; the problem is adding the card to Google Pay.

text: I'm not asking where the ATMs are, I found one fine. It just declined my cash withdrawal and I don't know why.
label: declined_cash_withdrawal
rationale: The customer rules out asking where ATMs are and reports a declined withdrawal.

text: It's not a card payment I'm worried about, it's a direct debit I don't recognise. Some company is taking £12 every month.
label: direct_debit_payment_not_recognised
rationale: The customer says it is not a card payment but a direct debit they don't recognise.

text: I'm not asking how to verify my identity, I did that ages ago. Now the app wants proof of where my savings came from, what counts?
label: verify_source_of_funds
rationale: Identity verification is already done; the customer is being asked to prove the source of their funds.

text: I don't need the steps for verifying my identity, I just want to understand why you need my passport at all.
label: why_verify_identity
rationale: The customer asks why verification is needed, not how to do it.

text: I don't need instructions on how to verify my identity, I've followed them five times and it keeps rejecting my selfie.
label: unable_to_verify_identity
rationale: The customer already knows the steps and keeps failing verification, which is unable_to_verify_identity.

text: My card payment wasn't declined, it went through in dollars, but the exchange rate you applied is way worse than the real one.
label: card_payment_wrong_exchange_rate
rationale: The payment went through, so it was not declined; the complaint is the exchange rate on a card payment.

text: I'm not complaining about the ATM fee, that's fine. The exchange rate on my cash withdrawal in Thailand was terrible though, why?
label: wrong_exchange_rate_for_cash_withdrawal
rationale: The ATM fee is accepted; the complaint is the exchange rate applied to a cash withdrawal abroad.

text: My card hasn't gone missing in the post, it arrived today. I just can't figure out how to activate it.
label: activate_my_card
rationale: The card has arrived, so card_arrival does not apply; the customer needs to activate it.

text: I'm not asking about typical delivery times. I ordered my card three weeks ago and it still hasn't turned up, can you track it?
label: card_arrival
rationale: The customer rules out a general delivery-time question and wants to track a card that is overdue.

text: My PIN isn't blocked or anything, it works fine, I'd just like to change it to something easier to remember.
label: change_pin
rationale: The PIN is not blocked; the customer only wants to change it.

text: This isn't a normal PIN change request. I typed it wrong three times and now it's blocked, how do I unblock it??
label: pin_blocked
rationale: The customer says it is not an ordinary PIN change; the PIN is blocked after wrong attempts.

text: I'm not asking about top-up fees, I want to know the maximum amount I'm allowed to top up in one go.
label: top_up_limits
rationale: Fees are ruled out; the question is about the maximum top-up amount.

text: I'm not asking whether I can deposit cheques, I already paid one in on Monday and my balance still hasn't changed.
label: balance_not_updated_after_cheque_or_cash_deposit
rationale: The customer is not asking whether cheques are accepted; a cheque already deposited has not updated the balance.

text: It's not a pending transfer, it's my card top-up that's been stuck on pending since this morning.
label: pending_top_up
rationale: The customer says it is not a transfer; the thing stuck on pending is a top-up.

text: My card wasn't stolen, it's still in my wallet, but I think I typed my card details into a phishing site. Should I freeze it?
label: compromised_card
rationale: The customer still has the card but thinks the details were exposed, which is a compromised card, not a lost or stolen one.

text: I don't want to close my account, I just lost my card on the bus last night and need it blocked asap.
label: lost_or_stolen_card
rationale: Closing the account is ruled out; the customer lost their card.

text: I'm not asking about the limits on disposable cards, I just want to make one. Where do I create a disposable virtual card?
label: get_disposable_virtual_card
rationale: Limits are ruled out; the customer wants to create a disposable virtual card.

text: My physical card works perfectly, the problem is the virtual card, it doesn't work on any website I try.
label: virtual_card_not_working
rationale: The physical card is said to work; the virtual card is the one failing.

text: This isn't a failed transfer, I can't even start one. The app says I'm not allowed to add my brother as a payee.
label: beneficiary_not_allowed
rationale: No transfer was attempted; the customer cannot add a payee, which is beneficiary_not_allowed.

text: I'm not trying to request a new refund. The shop already approved one two weeks ago and it's still not in my account.
label: Refund_not_showing_up
rationale: A new refund request is ruled out; an approved refund has not appeared in the account.

text: Not asking about ATMs abroad, I mean the account itself. Can I keep using the app if I move to Portugal?
label: country_support
rationale: ATMs are ruled out; the customer asks whether the service works in another country.

text: My card itself is fine, chip and PIN works every time, it's only contactless that does nothing when I tap.
label: contactless_not_working
rationale: The card works with chip and PIN, so only contactless is failing.

text: My new card arrived yesterday, but after typing the PIN wrong three times at the shop it now says my PIN is blocked.
label: pin_blocked
rationale: The card arrival is background; the actual problem is a blocked PIN after wrong attempts.

text: The transfer I cancelled last week was sorted fine. Now I just want to know how long a normal transfer to a UK account takes to arrive.
label: transfer_timing
rationale: The cancellation is resolved; the request is about how long transfers take.

text: Refund from the shop showed up fine, all sorted. Different question: how do I create a disposable virtual card for online shopping?
label: get_disposable_virtual_card
rationale: The refund is explicitly resolved; the ask is how to get a disposable virtual card.

text: I lost my card last month and the replacement finally came today. How do I activate it so I can start using it?
label: activate_my_card
rationale: The loss is past context; the customer wants to activate the replacement card.

text: Google Pay on my phone works fine, but the physical card itself has stopped working, terminals keep saying they can't read the chip.
label: card_not_working
rationale: Google Pay is mentioned as working; the fault is with the physical card.

text: My salary transfer landed in my balance fine this morning. What I actually need is to update my home address because I've moved.
label: edit_personal_details
rationale: The transfer and balance are fine; the request is to change personal details.

text: The ATM gave me exactly the right amount of cash, no issue there, but I got charged a fee for the withdrawal which I wasn't expecting.
label: cash_withdrawal_charge
rationale: The cash amount was correct; the complaint is about a withdrawal fee.

text: An ATM in Lisbon swallowed my card last week, but that's been dealt with and a replacement is ordered. How long does delivery usually take?
label: card_delivery_estimate
rationale: The swallowed card is resolved; the question is about delivery time for the new card.

text: Verified my ID no problem when I signed up. Now the app wants me to prove where my money comes from, what documents do I send?
label: verify_source_of_funds
rationale: Identity verification is done; the request concerns proving source of funds.

text: Contactless was acting up last month but it's fine now. Today I spotted a direct debit from a company I've never heard of.
label: direct_debit_payment_not_recognised
rationale: The contactless issue is resolved; the concern is an unrecognised direct debit.

text: I swapped some pounds to euros in the app yesterday, worked fine. Where can I check what exchange rate you're using right now?
label: exchange_rate
rationale: The in-app exchange is done; the customer asks where to see the current rate.

text: Topping up by bank transfer this morning was free, great. So why did the top up I did with my debit card cost me a fee?
label: top_up_by_card_charge
rationale: The bank transfer top-up is a comparison; the fee complaint is about the card top-up.

text: Forgot my passcode last week but reset it and got back in. Now I just want to close my account completely, how do I do that?
label: terminate_account
rationale: The passcode problem is resolved; the request is to close the account.

text: The card payment that was pending all weekend finally went through, but now there are two identical entries. I've been charged twice for it.
label: transaction_charged_twice
rationale: The pending status has cleared; the issue is a duplicate charge.

text: My card is safe in my wallet, it's my phone that got nicked on the bus. How do I stop someone getting into my banking app?
label: lost_or_stolen_phone
rationale: The card is explicitly safe; the phone was stolen and app access is the worry.

text: Changed my PIN at an ATM yesterday with no problem. Today a different ATM declined my withdrawal, what's going on?
label: declined_cash_withdrawal
rationale: The PIN change is completed background; the problem is a declined ATM withdrawal.

text: My virtual card works perfectly for online stuff. I'd like to order a physical card as well, what are the options and how much does it cost?
label: order_physical_card
rationale: The virtual card works fine; the customer wants to order a physical card and asks about cost.

text: Last month a transfer failed and I had to redo it. This time it shows completed, but my landlord says the money still hasn't reached him.
label: transfer_not_received_by_recipient
rationale: The failed transfer was in the past; the current transfer completed but the recipient has not received it.

text: Took cash out in Prague, the amount was right, but the exchange rate on that withdrawal is way worse than what the app showed me.
label: wrong_exchange_rate_for_cash_withdrawal
rationale: The cash amount was correct; the complaint is the rate applied to the withdrawal.

text: My top up went through fine and the money's there. But a card payment at a restaurant got reversed back to my account and I don't know why.
label: reverted_card_payment?
rationale: The top-up is fine; it is a card payment that was reverted.

text: The cheque I deposited cleared into my balance last week, no worries. Separately, can I top up my account using cash?
label: top_up_by_cash_or_cheque
rationale: The deposit has cleared; the question is whether cash top-ups are possible.

text: I already know how to top up with my card, done it loads. What's the maximum I'm allowed to top up in one go?
label: top_up_limits
rationale: The how-to is known; the question is about top-up limits.

text: My ID check finally went through yesterday after a few failed tries. Just curious though, why do you need to verify my identity at all?
label: why_verify_identity
rationale: The failed attempts are resolved; the customer asks why verification is needed.

text: Card got delivered and it's working. Quick one, is it a Visa or a Mastercard? I can't see it anywhere in the app.
label: visa_or_mastercard
rationale: Delivery is done; the question is about the card network.

text: The transfer fee last time was annoying but I paid it. Now my transfer to my brother just got declined with no reason given.
label: declined_transfer
rationale: The fee is past background; the current issue is a declined transfer.

text: The disposable card worked for that one purchase exactly as expected. How do I get a normal virtual card I can keep using?
label: getting_virtual_card
rationale: The disposable card is past context; the customer wants a regular reusable virtual card.

text: My pending top up from Monday finally cleared. Can I set up auto top-up so it refills whenever my balance drops below 20 quid?
label: automatic_top_up
rationale: The pending top-up has cleared; the request is to set up automatic top-ups.

text: Thought I'd lost my card yesterday but found it in my coat pocket. Now tap to pay won't work anywhere, chip and PIN is fine though.
label: contactless_not_working
rationale: The card was found; the problem is contactless payments failing.

text: My card is still in my wallet so it isn't lost, but I think the details got skimmed at a petrol station. What should I do?
label: compromised_card
rationale: The customer still has the card; they suspect its details were stolen.

text: My card works fine at the moment, no issues at all, but it expires next month. Will a new one be sent out automatically?
label: card_about_to_expire
rationale: The card is explicitly working; the question is about replacement before expiry.

text: My PIN got blocked last week but it's unblocked now. I'd like to change it to something I'll actually remember this time.
label: change_pin
rationale: The block is resolved; the customer wants to change their PIN.

text: Cash withdrawals with my card work fine, took some out this morning. But paying for a hotel online just got declined twice.
label: declined_card_payment
rationale: Withdrawals work; the problem is a declined online card payment.

text: I get why you need ID checks, that's fine. But the verification keeps rejecting my passport photo, I've tried five times now.
label: unable_to_verify_identity
rationale: The reason for verification is accepted; the issue is verification repeatedly failing.

text: I've already got my disposable virtual card set up, easy enough. How many times can I use it before it stops working?
label: disposable_card_limits
rationale: The card is already created; the question is about its usage limits.

text: My bank transfer yesterday showed up in my balance straight away. But the cash I deposited this morning still isn't showing at all.
label: balance_not_updated_after_cheque_or_cash_deposit
rationale: The bank transfer is a working comparison; the balance problem is with the cash deposit.

text: Put my card in the cashpoint at the petrol station, it whirred for ages and then the slot just stayed shut. It never came back out.
label: card_swallowed
rationale: The ATM kept the card, so this is card_swallowed; the card itself malfunctioning is not the issue.

text: Messed up my number at the till three times in a row and now the machine says no more attempts allowed. How do I unlock it?
label: pin_blocked
rationale: Repeated wrong PIN entries have locked the PIN; the payment failing is a symptom, not the request.

text: Someone nicked my mobile off the table at the pub last night and your app is on it. Can they get into my money?
label: lost_or_stolen_phone
rationale: The stolen item is the phone and the worry is app access, not a missing card.

text: Lost my old phone last week but that's sorted, I've got a new one. Problem is I cant remember the code I set to get into your app.
label: passcode_forgotten
rationale: The lost phone is already resolved; the actual request is a forgotten app passcode.

text: I've switched everything over to another bank now, so I'd like to be done with you completely. What's the process?
label: terminate_account
rationale: Being 'done with you completely' after switching banks means closing the account, not cancelling a transfer.

text: Really liking the new look of the app! Quick one though, my son is 14, is he allowed to have his own account with you?
label: age_limit
rationale: The praise is filler; the question is whether a 14-year-old meets the minimum age.

text: I ordered my card nearly three weeks ago and the post still hasn't brought anything. Can you find out where it's got to?
label: card_arrival
rationale: An already-ordered card is overdue and the customer wants it tracked, rather than a general delivery-time estimate.

text: Just requested the plastic version. Roughly how many days before the postman should be dropping it through my door?
label: card_delivery_estimate
rationale: The card is already ordered and the question is how long delivery takes, not how to order.

text: Need some notes for the taxi. Is there a particular kind of cash machine I should look for that'll take your card?
label: atm_support
rationale: The customer asks which cash machines accept the card, which is ATM support rather than merchant acceptance.

text: I typed my card number into a website that turned out to be dodgy. Card's still in my wallet but I'm worried someone has the details now.
label: compromised_card
rationale: The card is still in hand but its details may be stolen, which matches compromised_card.

text: My bag was snatched on the tube this morning and my purse with your card inside went with it. What do I do?
label: lost_or_stolen_card
rationale: The physical card itself was stolen, so this is lost_or_stolen_card, not details compromised while still held.

text: There's £200 taken out from a machine in Leeds on Saturday, but I was at home in Bristol all weekend and never went near one.
label: cash_withdrawal_not_recognised
rationale: The unrecognised transaction is a cash machine withdrawal, not a card purchase.

text: Some company I've never heard of is pulling £15 from my account on the 1st of every month under a mandate I never agreed to.
label: direct_debit_payment_not_recognised
rationale: A recurring mandate-based collection is a direct debit, not a card payment.

text: Card arrived yesterday and works great, thanks. Only thing is the cafe this morning took £3.40 from me two separate times for one coffee.
label: transaction_charged_twice
rationale: The card arriving is just context; the actual problem is a single purchase being charged twice.

text: Machine gave me £60. I asked for £100. Account shows the full £100 gone.
label: wrong_amount_of_cash_received
rationale: The ATM dispensed less cash than was debited, which is wrong amount received, not a fee.

text: My card pays fine in shops, but every cashpoint I try today says it can't complete the request and gives me nothing.
label: declined_cash_withdrawal
rationale: The card works for purchases, so the issue is specifically ATM withdrawals being declined.

text: Got euros out of a machine in Madrid and the pounds you took off me don't match what the rate was that day at all.
label: wrong_exchange_rate_for_cash_withdrawal
rationale: The disputed conversion is on a cash withdrawal from a machine, not a card payment.

text: The conversion you used for my dinner bill in Prague looks way off, I paid a lot more in pounds than Google said I should have.
label: card_payment_wrong_exchange_rate
rationale: The customer disputes the rate applied to a specific foreign card payment, not asking what rates are in general.

text: Managed to update my address myself, cheers. Now I'd like one of those card numbers that only works for a single purchase, for shopping on sketchy sites.
label: get_disposable_virtual_card
rationale: The address change is done; the request is to get a single-use virtual card.

text: Those throwaway card numbers in the app, how many times can I actually use one before it stops working?
label: disposable_card_limits
rationale: The question is about the usage limit of disposable cards, not a card that is currently failing.

text: When I hold my card against the reader nothing happens, so I always end up putting it in the slot and typing my number.
label: contactless_not_working
rationale: Chip and PIN works, so only the tap-to-pay function is failing.

text: I'd rather just wave my iPhone at the till than carry the card around. How do I get it set up on there?
label: apple_pay_or_google_pay
rationale: The customer wants to add the card to their phone wallet, not report broken contactless.

text: The four numbers I tap in at shops are my old house number and I'd like something different. How do I swap them?
label: change_pin
rationale: The house number is only where the PIN came from; the request is to change the card PIN, not the address.

text: Got married last month, so the surname showing on my profile isn't right anymore. Can I get that fixed?
label: edit_personal_details
rationale: The customer wants to update their name on the account, which is a personal details change.

text: Top-up went through fine, no problem there. But now you're asking me for payslips to show where the £8,000 came from. What exactly do you need?
label: verify_source_of_funds
rationale: The top-up worked; the real question is what proof of the money's origin is required.

text: Why on earth does a card app need a photo of my passport and a selfie from me? Seems a bit much tbh.
label: why_verify_identity
rationale: The customer is asking why identity checks are required, not how to complete them.

text: Sent my driving licence photo five times now and every single time it bounces back rejected. I'm going round in circles.
label: unable_to_verify_identity
rationale: The customer is already trying to verify and it keeps failing, rather than asking how to start.

text: Can I walk in somewhere and hand over paper notes or a cheque from my nan to add money to my balance?
label: top_up_by_cash_or_cheque
rationale: This asks whether cash or cheque top-ups are possible, not about a deposit that hasn't shown up.

text: I'd love the account to refill itself from my main bank card whenever it runs low, so I never get caught short at the till.
label: automatic_top_up
rationale: Refilling automatically when the balance is low is exactly an automatic top-up.

text: The shop says they sent my money back for the returned trainers ten days ago, but there's still no sign of it on my side.
label: Refund_not_showing_up
rationale: The merchant says the refund has been issued but it hasn't arrived, so there is nothing new to request.

text: I paid for a hotel last week and today the money just reappeared in my account without me asking for a refund or anything. Why?
label: reverted_card_payment?
rationale: A card payment came back unprompted and the customer wants to know why, which is a reverted payment rather than a missing refund.

text: Trying to save my landlord's bank details so I can pay him, but the app just won't let me add him as someone to pay.
label: beneficiary_not_allowed
rationale: The failure is in adding the payee, before any transfer is attempted.

text: Sent this month's rent to totally the wrong person by accident five minutes ago. Can I pull it back before it lands?
label: cancel_transfer
rationale: The customer wants to reverse a mistaken transfer, not chase one that hasn't arrived.

text: Your phone line kept me on hold for forty minutes, which is ridiculous. Anyway, if I send money to my mum in Spain today, when will she have it?
label: transfer_timing
rationale: The hold-time complaint is venting; the question is how long an international transfer takes to arrive.

text: I did get the right amount of cash, so no issue there, but Tuesday's withdrawal is still showing as not completed in the app.
label: pending_cash_withdrawal
rationale: The customer rules out a wrong amount; the issue is the withdrawal still showing as pending.
